name: Cicera
description: Cicera (also known as Cicera Bigia or Ciccera Biccera) is an Italian fishing card game closely related to Scopa and Scopone, played in the province of Brescia using a unique 52-card Bresciane deck. The game is the reason why Bresciane playing cards are made with 52 cards rather than the standard Italian 40 cards.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing cards from the table and achieving specific card combinations. Points awarded for most cards, most cards in a specific suit, and capturing the seven of coins/diamonds (settebello).
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal 12 cards to each player, 4 cards face-up to table
2. If 3+ Aces on table, reshuffle and redeal
3. Player to dealer's right plays first, turns proceed anticlockwise
4. On turn: Play one card to capture matching table card(s) by value
5. If capture made: Take captured card(s) and played card as trick
6. If no capture: Played card remains on table
7. Continue until all cards are played
8. Last player to capture takes remaining table cards
keyRules: Must capture if possible - cannot play a card that could capture without capturing
Can capture single card of matching value OR multiple cards summing to played card's value
A sweep (cappotto) occurs when capturing all table cards at once
Last player to capture any cards takes remaining table cards at end
Play is anticlockwise (traditional for Italian games)

strategy.basic: Focus on capturing high-value cards and the settebello. Try to make sweeps when possible. Keep track of which cards have been played.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards to track remaining captures. Set up sweeps by leaving specific combinations on the table. Balance capturing now versus setting up future captures.
strategy.advanced: Complex probability calculations for capture opportunities. Track suit distribution for majority bonuses. Sophisticated sweep setup requiring multi-turn planning.
tips: The settebello (7 of coins) is worth a full point - prioritize it
Sweeps (cappotto) can swing the game significantly
Track which high cards have been played
Balance immediate captures with setting up future plays
Remember which cards your partner has played in partnership games
